meta.description: Restaurant order taking from a phone or tablet: floor map, bill splitting, statuses, options and comments. Guests order from the table, waiters take orders on their own device. 14 days free.
meta.ogTitle: Restaurant Order Taking — Guest and Waiter
meta.ogDescription: A guest at the table or a waiter on a phone — the order hits the kitchen instantly. Floor map, bill splitting, statuses, options and comments.

hero.headline: Orders from the table —
hero.sub: Guests order at the table or waiters from any device — straight to the kitchen. Floor plan, bill splitting.

tablet.alt: Tablet with an open order: dish list and order actions — change table, split order, add discount

scan.heading: Set up your order-taking system
scan.sub: Scan a paper menu or a PDF — AI recognizes dishes, prices and categories. Connect a tablet on the floor and start taking orders from the tables.

subFeatures.heading: An order list next to the floor map.
subFeatures.body: All active orders are shown on the right: status, total, time placed and item count. On the left is the floor map: tables are color-coded by status — empty, occupied, needs attention. Tapping a table opens its order, tapping a card opens the detailed view. No switching between screens.
bullets: Floor map: tables color-coded by order status.
Order list alongside — total, time and item count.
Tapping a table opens the order or creates a new one.

image.alt: Tablet at a waiter station: an order list and a floor map with color-coded tables

subFeatures.heading: The order card: statuses, duplicating and removing — with one tap.
subFeatures.body: Every item has its own status (Pending / Cooking / Ready / Served) — the kitchen and the waiter see the same picture in real time. Tapping the dot opens an action menu: change status, duplicate the item with the same modifiers and options, or remove it. Everything happens right inside the order card.
bullets: Per-item status: Pending / Cooking / Ready / Served.
Duplicate an item with one tap — same options included.
Remove an item right from the order card.

image.alt: Tablet with a detailed order card: dish statuses, duplicating and removing items

subFeatures.heading: Bill splitting for when guests pay separately.
subFeatures.body: Guests decide to pay separately — check the items that go to the new bill; the rest stay on the current one. The system shows both totals immediately. One tap on "Split order" — and you have two independent orders with correct totals, both staying on their tables.
bullets: Select items to split using checkboxes.
The new and remaining bill totals appear instantly.
One tap — and the order is split with no manual math.

image.alt: Tablet on a restaurant table: splitting the bill between guests

subFeatures.heading: Adding items from a phone — in three steps.
subFeatures.body: Waiters aren't tied to a single device: they open the order-taking screen on their own phone and add an item in three steps — pick a category, pick a dish, pick options (size, doneness, extra sauces and ingredients). The price recalculates automatically. A kitchen comment is added at the last step.
bullets: Options (size, add-ons, ingredients) with pricing in one tap.
A comment field at the final step.

image.alt: Four phones showing the steps of adding an item to an order: category, dish, size, comment

faq.sub: What restaurateurs ask about order taking in IQ Rest. If your question isn't listed — message us on WhatsApp.

items.q: Can several waiters work simultaneously from different devices?
items.a: Yes. Each waiter connects their own device and sees the same tables, orders and statuses in real time. A change made by one appears instantly for the others — no conflicts or locking.

items.q: Can waiters use their personal devices?
items.a: Yes. The orders screen runs in the browser — nothing to install. A phone or tablet connects with a six-digit code from the dashboard, and access is revoked with one tap at the end of the shift.

items.q: Can I add required options to dishes (size, doneness)?
items.a: Yes. A dish can have any number of option groups — required ("Size": Small / Medium / Big) and optional ("Doneness": rare / medium / well done). Options affect the price. With a required group, the system asks for a choice — eliminating mistakes.

items.q: Can I add comments and extra items to a dish?
items.a: Yes. The last step has a comment field ("no onions", "nut allergy"). Extras are set up as priced options ("+ BBQ sauce", "+ Bread"). Comments appear on the kitchen display, highlighted in color.
